summary: Michael J. Sweet was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under Ngawang Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Legden, Khenpo Sangye Tenzin, Richard Hugh Robinson, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, later serving there in psychiatry.
Michael J. Tetreault is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He completed his Master of Arts at San Diego State University under the supervision of Sandra A. Wawrytko.

Michael J. Walsh is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Cape Town and the University of California, Santa Barbara, completing his doctorate under William F. Powell.

Michael Janda is a linguist and Indologist who studied under Jochem Schindler and Heiner Eichner, earning a PhD from the University of Vienna and his Habilitation from the University of Zurich. He held posts at Zurich and the University of Münster.

Michael Jansen was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Bonn, RWTH Aachen, Rome, Delhi, and the Archaeological Survey of India. His positions included architecture dean at RWTH Aachen, founding rector at GUtech, and president of Research Centre Indian Ocean.

Michael K. Jerryson was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Harold Scheub, and later held faculty posts at Eckerd College and Youngstown State University.
Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

Michael L. Walter worked in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A student of Larry Moses, he served as a research fellow at Lumbini International Research Institute and held editorial consultant and cataloger posts at Indiana University.

Michael M. Broido is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge from circa 1963 to 1970 and held an academic post at the University of Oxford.
Michael Oppitz is a scholar of Tibetology. He held a post at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin from circa 1987 to 1988 and served as director at the University of Zurich from circa 1990 to 2008.
Michael P. Berman is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Brock University and worked as the managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.

Michael Puett is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu, and has served on the faculty at Harvard University since circa 1994.

Michael Pye is a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology scholar. He studied at Cambridge and Leeds under Maurice Wiles, and held posts at the University of Leeds, University of Marburg, Lancaster University, and Otani University.

Michael Radich is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. Educated at Auckland, Harvard (PhD under Robert M. Gimello), and Kyoto, he held posts at Victoria University of Wellington, Kyoto, Hamburg, and was appointed professor at Heidelberg in 2018.

Michael Rostovtzeff was a historian and archaeologist of Central Asian and Iranian studies. Educated at Kyiv and St. Petersburg University, he held posts at Imperial St. Petersburg University, Bestuzhev Courses, Oxford, Wisconsin-Madison, and Yale.
Michael S. Drummond is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and was attested as a PhD candidate at Utrecht University.

Michael Schmidt is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held editorial and researcher positions at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and worked for the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland.

Michael Sheehy is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under Steven D. Goodman and held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia.
Michael Silverstein was a linguist who studied at Stuyvesant High School and Harvard University. He spent his academic career on the faculty at the University of Chicago from circa 1970 until 2020.

Michael Stanley-Baker is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned an MA at Indiana University under Stephen R. Bokenkamp. He has held positions at Pittsburgh, MPIWG, the University of Leipzig, and Nanyang Technological University.
